title: Inner product and vector noise
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and let $\rho\in[0,1]$. For every function $f:(\mathrm{Fin}\ n\to\Omega)\to V$ into a real inner product space $V$, every $v\in V$, and every $x\in\mathrm{Fin}\ n\to\Omega$, the inner product of $v$ with the vector-valued product noise average of $f$ at $x$ equals the scalar product noise average of the function $y\mapsto\langle v,f(y)\rangle$ at $x$.
hypotheses_covered: $V$ is a real inner product space
$\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
